evidence: io.lisp:2630: `(let* ((file (fnn-extent-register-at path base)) ...` registers before the verdict. On refusal (io.lisp:2639-2644) it only prints `checkpoint image refused reason=...`, clears, and returns `(values :refused 0)`. extent.lisp:141-145 says of fnn-extent-register-at: "a read-only descriptor held for the process's life".
fix: Unregister the file id and close its descriptor on the refusal path, or register only after fn-store-sco-image-open accepts the binding (pass the path and base to the check first).
reviewer: fnn-state-checkpoint-adopt-image (io.lisp:2630) calls fnn-extent-register-at before the verdict. On refusal (io.lisp:2639-2644) it clears and returns :refused without fnn-extent-close (extent.lisp:1225). extent.lisp:141-145 documents that the descriptor is held for the process's life. So one read-only fd per refused open stays open and can pin the replaced checkpoint's blocks until restart. It is bounded to one per open and happens only on a refused image.
scenario: The image binding does not match (a restored backup's checkpoint, or a store-identity mismatch). The open falls back to full replay, but the descriptor on the refused checkpoint file stays registered and open for the whole owner run, and nothing ever reads it. After the next publication replaces the checkpoint's name, that descriptor pins the old file's blocks on disk until restart.
title: A refused checkpoint history image still registers a file id whose read-only descriptor stays open for the process's life
